instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a 'lobbyist' as an individual paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying (with a 5-days-per-reporting-period trigger when duties are mixed), requires a person to be licensed and authorized to lobby (subject to limited exemptions), and provides only a narrow $500 verified-statement alternative, so paid lobbyists generally must be licensed/authorized to lobby.
A lobbyist license 'shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year,' which implies renewal on a biennial (24-month) cycle.

The statute separately requires lobbyists to obtain a license and principals to file a registration statement, with an additional separate written authorization linking a licensed lobbyist to a registered principal.

The lobbyist license application is required to include items like a social security number (or sworn statement of no SSN) and signature, but no photograph requirement appears in the application provisions.
Public officials and legislative employees are expressly not subject to multiple lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.

Agencies that file a statement under §13.695 and officials named in it are exempt from several key lobbying requirements (including licensing/registration/reporting sections) except as otherwise provided in §13.695.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text specifies a 10-day change-notice rule for agencies under §13.695(2) and a 15-day topic-reporting rule for principals under §13.67(1), but it does not state any lobbyist-side deadline to notify the commission of changes in the lobbyist’s own license/registration information.

Wisconsin uses lobbyist 'licensing' (§13.63) and principal 'registration' (§13.64) plus written authorization (§13.65), but the bundled sections do not specify a numeric deadline (days after first lobbying) by which the lobbyist must file the license application; only principals have a 'within 10 days after exceeding $500' registration trigger (§13.64(1)).
